title: Microsoft Purview: apply a retention policy to Microsoft Planner content
summary: The briefing accurately reports the launched roadmap item alongside Microsoft's documentation that still says Planner retention is unsupported. Its general retention controls and licensing are supported, and the Planner-specific gaps remain unconfirmed after targeted searches. Minor corrections concern the wording about hold duration and a role-assignment checklist step not represented in the controls table.

claims.claim: The general retention-policy creation route is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies. Select New retention policy to start the Create retention policy configuration

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> identifies the cmdlet for creating a retention policy and its naming parameter.
claims.quote: Use the New-RetentionCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create new retention policies and new retention label policies in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal. The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the retention policy.

claims.claim: The cmdlet is used in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The -ModernGroupLocation parameter selects Microsoft 365 Groups.
claims.quote: The ModernGroupLocation parameter specifies the Microsoft 365 Groups to include in the policy.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference names no Planner-specific location parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Planner retention policy New-RetentionCompliancePolicy PlannerLocation Microsoft 365 Groups retention supported plan types'; searched the fetched New-RetentionCompliancePolicy reference for Planner and read its location parameters. No Planner-specific parameter found.

claims.claim: A Planner plan lives inside a container.
claims.quote: Within Planner, each Plan is inside a container, and access to the plan is defined by the container.

claims.claim: Members of a Microsoft 365 Group can see the plan held in that group.
claims.quote: For example, if the Plan is inside a Modern Group, then the members of the Group can see the contents of the Plan.

claims.claim: Basic-plan task data is stored in Azure.
claims.quote: The data of a basic plan, such as the titles and descriptions of tasks, are stored in Azure, encrypted at rest and in transit.

claims.claim: Planner file attachments are stored in SharePoint.
claims.quote: File attachments are stored in SharePoint and Conversations are stored in Exchange. (Some features, like attachments and conversations, are only available on certain container types.)

claims.claim: Planner conversations and task comments are stored in Exchange.
claims.quote: Attachments on tasks are stored in SharePoint and comments are stored in Exchange.

claims.claim: General retention settings can retain only.
claims.quote: Retain-only: Retain content forever or for a specified period of time.

claims.claim: General delete-only retention settings permanently delete content after a specified period.
claims.quote: Delete-only: Permanently delete content after a specified period of time.

claims.claim: General retention settings can retain content and then delete it.
claims.quote: Retain and then delete: Retain content for a specified period of time and then permanently delete it.

claims.claim: Planner's Purview page documents eDiscovery holds for Planner plans.
claims.quote: For Planner data, select the SharePoint site associated with the plan and check the box for Planner tasks.

claims.claim: When a hold is applied, the Planner task is not deleted.
claims.quote: When a hold is applied, the task won't be deleted and is copied to the Preservation Hold Library of the SharePoint site.

claims.claim: The held Planner task is copied to the SharePoint site's Preservation Hold Library.
claims.quote: When a hold is applied, the task won't be deleted and is copied to the Preservation Hold Library of the SharePoint site.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery hold is not a retention policy.
claims.quote: Although retention settings and holds that you create with an eDiscovery case can both prevent data from being permanently deleted, they are designed for different scenarios.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery hold has no retention period.
claims.quote: The start and end of the preservation period isn't configurable but dependent on individual administrator actions, without an option to automatically delete content when the hold is released.
claims.fix: Replace 'A hold is not a retention policy and has no retention period.' with 'An eDiscovery hold is not a retention policy: its preservation period has no configurable start or end and depends on administrator actions.' The distinction is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention#when-to-use-retention-policies-and-retention-labels-or-ediscovery-holds.
